headline: Highest risk is capability conflict: Aider can write/commit to a shared git repo while ComfyUI is read-only and offline, so prompt-injection and leakage are limited but repo races remain.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider can read/write repo files and parse stdin/stdout, so malicious content in shared files could influence it. ComfyUI has no filesystem write or stdin/stdout surface, so it is not a strong injector. The bridge is mainly manual or repo-based, making the pathway possible but limited.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository files
IF a human copies ComfyUI-generated text into Aider prompts or tracked files
mitigations: Keep ComfyUI outputs out of the shared repo
Review repo diffs before Aider applies them
Use separate worktrees for the two agents
Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted file content where possible

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history and can egress broadly, but ComfyUI is offline by default and does not read the filesystem. There is no clear shared sensitive-data channel in the profiles, so leakage is limited to unusual manual transfer of code or secrets into Aider.
conditions: IF sensitive code or secrets are manually copied into Aider prompts
IF ComfyUI is configured to call external APIs with user data
mitigations: Avoid pasting secrets into Aider
Store secrets outside the repo
Keep ComfyUI offline unless needed
Use separate credentials per tool
Audit any exported artifacts before sharing

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider has unrestricted filesystem write and modify_git_state, while ComfyUI has no write or git capabilities. The conflict is asymmetric, but Aider's shared-state model via a git repo means concurrent edits can still collide in default multi-instance use. ComfyUI does not add write contention, so this is not high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same git working tree
IF Aider runs concurrently with another writer to the repo
mitigations: Use one writer per repo at a time
Create separate branches or worktrees
Require manual merge review
Pause ComfyUI jobs while Aider commits

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider can generate code changes, but ComfyUI has no write or action-taking authority and no documented pipeline that consumes Aider output as authoritative. Without a downstream executor, the main risk is a human or script reusing Aider output, which is a limited cascade rather than a default failure mode.
conditions: IF a human or script feeds Aider output directly into ComfyUI workflows
IF generated text is treated as authoritative without review
mitigations: Require manual review of Aider output
Do not auto-import generated configs into ComfyUI
Validate any workflow JSON before execution
Keep execution scripts separate from chat output

E_compliance.rationale: Aider handles source code, git history, and provider API keys, while ComfyUI handles images and model assets. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so compliance risk is mainly local retention or secret-handling hygiene rather than a documented breach pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared repo or image assets
IF either agent is used with data subject to stricter retention rules
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Separate model assets from source repositories
Rotate any exposed API keys
Apply local retention rules to exports
Document data-class handling per tool
